evidence: Yuri Milner's own website states that in 2012 he and his wife Julia partnered with Sergey Brin, Priscilla Chan and Mark Zuckerberg, and Anne Wojcicki to launch the Breakthrough Prizes.
Milner's own website names Anne Wojcicki among the co-founders of the Breakthrough Prizes launched with him and his wife in 2012.
Both are named on Yuri Milner's own website as partners in the 2012 launch of the Breakthrough Prizes, alongside Milner, Chan and Zuckerberg.
TechCrunch reports that New Wave, the European seed fund Xavier Niel co-founded in 2020, attracted Yuri Milner of DST among its high-profile limited partners.
Alphabet's 2026 proxy lists both Larry Page and Sergey Brin as Co-Founders and directors since 1998, and quotes their joint 2004 IPO letter to shareholders.
Skip Capital's own site describes Scott Farquhar as 'Co founder of Atlassian'; Mike Cannon-Brookes is Atlassian's other co-founder and CEO. They founded and still jointly control the company.
Facebook's 2014 acquisition release names Jan Koum as WhatsApp co-founder and CEO; Signal's 2018 launch post names Brian Acton as the co-founder of WhatsApp. Same company, same founding team.
Forbes reports that Sean Parker 'joined the board of Daniel Ek's Spotify', placing the two on the same board at the company Ek founded.

Loam Bio, the Australian soil-carbon company, appears on both Grok Ventures' own portfolio page (first invested 2019) and Horizons Ventures' own portfolio data (2019). Two independent family-office vehicles in the same small company in the same year.

Beyond co-founding Atlassian, Grok Ventures and Skip Capital both publish Brighte, Neara and Zoomo among their own holdings, so the two family offices co-invest repeatedly in Australian climate and infrastructure software.
Horizons Ventures' own portfolio data and Skip Capital's own technology page both list Airwallex, Harrison.ai and Kimia, so the two vehicles overlap in Australian medical AI and cross-border fintech.

Spore.Bio, the Paris instant-microbiology startup, appears on Point72 Ventures' own portfolio page (first invested 2025, Series A) and on Kima Ventures' own portfolio page. A rare direct overlap between a US hedge-fund venture arm and a French angel vehicle.
Arena, the enterprise-AI company, appears both in QuantumLight's own portfolio table and on Skip Capital's own technology investments page.
Airbnb appears on both Aglae Ventures' own companies list and Bezos Expeditions' own Selected Investments list, so the two family vehicles hold the same asset.
Spotify appears on Aglae Ventures' own companies list and in Horizons Ventures' own portfolio data (2009), placing both family vehicles on the same early cap table.

Twitter appears on Bezos Expeditions' own Selected Investments list while Twitter's final proxy shows Jack Dorsey as a 2.4% holder and co-founder, so both had equity in the same company pre-take-private.
